name: Thailand

latest_census.notes: 2020 Population and Housing Census (B.E. 2563; enumeration slipped into 2021-22). UNSD paper 's05-06-THA.pdf' snippet: religion was among the variables collected. The 2010 census metadata (IHSN catalog 4405) lists 'age, sex, religion, nationality, speaking languages' -- so NATIONALITY is asked, not ethnicity; treat ethnicity as not asked. A Thai-language search result says 2020 census reports were produced at provincial/regional as well as national level, but no provincial religion or language table surfaced as a URL. Note the repo's recorded finding that nso.go.th / catalog.nso.go.th answer HTTP 418 and data.go.th 403 to this project's fetcher, and that CLEAR Global's HDX notes claim 2000 was the only census for which language data were made public.

subnational_sources.title: Nationality, religion, and language data for the provinces of Thailand
subnational_sources.publisher: Wikipedia (compiled from NSO census publications, per the article's subject; sourcing unverified)
subnational_sources.evidence: Search snippet: 'In both 1970 and 2000, almost every Thai province's population was Buddhist-majority ... exceptions being Narathiwat, Pattani, Satun, and Yala'; 'Mae Hong Son's population was composed of a majority of hill tribe language speakers in both 1990 and 2000'; nationality by province for 1970 and 2000. So the article carries per-province religion (1970/1990/2000), language (1990/2000) and nationality tables. Whether it also carries 2010 figures is not visible in the snippet. Wikidata item Q105821639 exists for the article. Province count in 2000 was fewer than today's 77 (Bueng Kan created 2011), so a handful of admin1 shapes will be unmatched or must be flagged.

subnational_sources.title: Thailand - Population and Housing Census 2010 (IHSN metadata record; NSO provincial reports)
subnational_sources.publisher: National Statistical Office, Thailand (record mirrored on IHSN)
subnational_sources.evidence: IHSN snippet: 'demographic data collected included ... age, sex, religion, nationality, speaking languages' and 'respondents could access census data via www.nso.go.th or http://popcensus.nso.go.th'. The 2010 questionnaire is at https://unstats.un.org/unsd/demographic/sources/census/quest/THA2010en.pdf. No URL for a provincial religion/language table surfaced in two targeted searches; the NSO hosts refuse this project's fetcher (recorded in SOURCES.md), so a runner would need the PDFs by another route.

tier_reason: The census asks religion and language (2010, 2020) and NSO publishes provincial reports, but no machine-readable provincial table surfaced and the NSO/data.go.th hosts refuse this project's fetcher; the one census-sourced provincial table that is reachable is a Wikipedia list article (HTML, latest year in snippet is 2000). Ethnicity is not asked (nationality is).
recommended_action: Have a runner read the Wikipedia list article 'Nationality, religion, and language data for the provinces of Thailand' and report which census years and how many provinces its religion and language tables carry; if a 2010 column is present, that is the admin1 build. Separately, declare ethnicity not_collected (census asks nationality). Do not re-try nso.go.th or data.go.th from the sandbox. The gdcatalog.go.th census-results entry is worth one look from a machine that can open it. Nothing found for the 928 admin2 districts.

summary: Thailand's census does ask religion and 'speaking languages' (2010 and 2020) and asks nationality rather than ethnicity, so ethnicity should be declared not_collected. The NSO publishes provincial reports, but no provincial religion or language table surfaced as a URL and the NSO and data.go.th hosts are recorded as refusing this project's fetcher. The realistic route is the Wikipedia list article 'Nationality, religion, and language data for the provinces of Thailand', which by its snippet carries per-province religion (1970/1990/2000) and language (1990/2000) tables from the censuses; a runner should read it and check for a 2010 column. A data.go.th survey dataset on religious adherents (CSV) is new but is a survey and not confirmed to be by province. Tier B; nothing for admin2.
